statements.r5-m10: At T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 the plain-prompt Olmo-3-1025-7B base commits within its first few tokens to one of two whole answer modes: answers that open on their own with a newline then 'Okay' are the cued mode, solving each problem about as often as cued answers do and having the same length, while the rest are the plain mode; the cue's +38.6 points is (1 - self-open share) x (self-opened accuracy - other accuracy), and nothing after the opening adds to it.
statements.r5-m10-rival: At T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 the cue's gain comes from self-checking deliberation (re-checks marked by 'Wait' / 'Hmm') that makes an answer robust to full-temperature sampling noise wherever in the answer it starts: the '\nOkay' opening is only the most common way into it, not a commitment made in the first few tokens, so plain answers that open tersely but later switch to self-checking recover most of the cued accuracy on the same problems.

experiments.experiment: Plain base, MATH-500 n = 500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, seed base 47,000,000 (as T3), with the self-open string '.\n\nOkay' prefilled after the plain prompt instead of the 3-token cue, grader v3, one sample. If the opening alone picks the whole mode, this scores like the 3-token cue (410/500).

other_prediction.why: In the mechanism, '.\n\nOkay' is the most common way into the self-checking register, and self-opened plain answers are as robust at T 1.0 as cued ones (D = 0.00); so prefilling it gives close to the cue's 410, a little lower because the register runs about 1.2x longer without the cue's push and has a few more cap hits at 16,384.

experiments.experiment: Rejection sampling on the base's own opening, no prefilled tokens: for each problem, draw up to 32 plain-prompt openings of at most 24 new tokens (T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, seed 47,000,000 + i + 10,000*j for draw j = 1..32) and keep the first whose text has '\nOkay' (newline then 'Okay') in its first 60 characters. Then continue that opening at the same setting to the 16,384-token cap (cap counted from the start of the answer, opening included), with the opening's own seed. If no draw self-opens, continue draw 1. Problems whose stored T3 row (plain base, seed base 47,000,000) already self-opens by the same test keep that row unchanged, so only the other ~332 problems are run. experiments.why: The mechanism says an answer that opens with '\nOkay' on its own is the cued mode as a whole, at cued accuracy (about 82 %) and cued length, so picking the base's own self-opening drafts should move the plain cell from 224 toward the cue's 410. The prediction is lower than 410 because about 10-15 % of problems never self-open in 32 draws (those fall back to the plain mode at about 26 %), and self-open propensity favours some problems over others.

other_prediction.why: Under the mechanism a self-opened plain answer has entered the self-checking register and is as robust at T 1.0 as a cued answer on the same problems (D = 0.00, AUROC 0.54 says the ~332 non-self-opened problems are of near-average difficulty), so the ~168 stored self-opened rows (~0.82, ~138 right) plus ~332 rejection-sampled self-opened continuations at cued-level accuracy (~0.81, slightly lowered by the longer plain register's extra cap hits, R = 1.21) give about the cued 410, a little below.

experiments.experiment: Plain prompt at T 1.0 with restart-on-terse decoding: a finished answer is rejected and resampled when its first 60 characters lack '\nOkay' AND its full text contains neither 'Wait' nor 'Hmm' (case-sensitive). There are up to 2 restarts, and the last attempt is kept if all are rejected. Cap-hit answers are kept as they are, with no restart. Attempt 0 reuses the stored T3 row for each problem, so only restarts are generated. experiments.why: The mechanism says T 1.0 robustness comes from self-checking, however it is entered: answers that self-open or later say 'Wait'/'Hmm' score about 0.5-0.8 against about 0.26 for terse ones (rival test gap +0.24). So resampling terse answers until a self-checking one appears should lift the plain T 1.0 cell from 224 to about 280.

other_prediction.why: If the opening sets the whole mode, then about 34% of answers self-open and score about 82%, and plain-mode answers score about 26%. That gives 224 = 168*0.82 + 332*0.26. Rejecting terse non-Okay answers (assuming about 43% of attempts are rejected, if about 35% of plain answers contain Wait/Hmm) and allowing up to 2 restarts raises the self-opened share of kept answers to about 0.52-0.54. Each converted problem gains about 0.56, so about 224 + 0.2*0.56*500, reduced a little for per-problem propensity and kept cap hits.
